headline: The KB describes the Gold Rewards Card's 0.025% both as a credit-card bonus that does not stack and as a separate relationship bonus that does, so $140 and $142 are both defensible corrections.

issues.summary: doc_013 calls the Gold Rewards Card's 0.025% a 'relationship bonus APY on top of the base rate'. doc_045 says credit-card bonuses DO stack with relationship bonuses. But doc_014 and doc_045's own example list the same 0.025% as a non-stacking credit-card bonus. The gold treats it as a credit-card bonus that loses to EcoCard's 0.6%.
evidence: doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_013: "As a Gold Rewards Card holder, you receive an additional 0.025% relationship bonus APY on top of the base rate."
doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_014 table: "| Gold Rewards Card | +0.025% |" under "Credit card APY bonuses"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045: "credit card APY bonuses DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as: ... Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products"
doc_045 example: Gold Rewards +0.025%, Platinum +0.15%, EcoCard +0.6% -> "The customer receives only the EcoCard bonus of +0.6%"
issues.why_it_matters: The customer explicitly asks for 'any other boosts that I'm missing'. An agent that also adds doc_013's relationship bonus computes 5.5 + 0.75 + 0.6 + 0.025 = 6.875% and credits 96000 x 1.775% / 12 = $142.00, which fails the hash (replayed: differs).
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite doc_013 to say its 0.025% is the Gold Rewards Card's credit-card APY bonus (subject to the highest-only rule), not a separate relationship bonus.

issues.summary: doc_013's worked example adds 5.5% + 0.025% and reports a total of 6.0%, which is a corrupted value. The customer's own mistaken belief is also 6.0%.
evidence: doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_013: "Base APY: 5.5% / Relationship bonus APY: +0.025% / Total APY with the bonus: 6.0%"
user instructions item 1: "so I should be at 6.0% APY"
issues.why_it_matters: A careful agent recomputes the sum, but the corrupted total seems to confirm the customer's wrong figure and could anchor a weaker agent.

solution_check: Gold Account base 5.5% (gold_account_001). Green checking + Gold is pairing 1 with a +0.75% boost (green_account_(checking)_001). Credit cards held: Platinum 0.15, Gold Rewards 0.025, EcoCard 0.6; the highest is EcoCard 0.6 (doc_045). Expected 6.85%. Actual 408 x 12 / 96000 = 5.1%. Difference 96000 x 1.75% / 12 = $140.00, which matches the gold. The open question is whether doc_013's 0.025% relationship bonus is a separate component; if it is, the answer is 6.875% and $142.00.
prior_note: The prior review flagged the same double description of the 0.025% as Minor. Because this customer asks for every missing boost, and doc_045 explicitly lets relationship bonuses stack, I rate the divergence Major, consistent with task_095.
notes: Grading-model bullets confirmed against the v1.0.1 snapshot. Both apply_savings_account_credit_6831 and submit_interest_discrepancy_report_7294 cast amounts with float(), and record ids embed f'{amount}' / f'{expected_apy}', so 33 and 33.0 hash identically, but any difference in value (even one cent) changes the hash. Gold read get_bank_account_transactions_9173 and get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 are allowlisted, so skipping either changes the hash. Monthly interest convention: the posted credits equal balance x APY / 12 exactly (simple, not daily-compounded), so the agent can infer the convention from the data. Replay: amount 140 (int) with actual_apy 5.1 gives the same hash as the gold. 142.00/6.875 gives a different hash. No Gold Account doc describes a generic multi-product relationship bonus; the only candidate is doc_013's card-holder bonus.
